keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Traikutakas. The page says only "The dominions of the Traikutakas further included Aparanta and northern Maharashtra" with coins "in southern Gujarat and southern Maharashtra". Cliopatria draws the Vakataka over 202 of these 368 cells from 451 and the Gupta Empire over 163 in 410-450, so the Traikutaka land overlaps those shapes; the Traikutaka dates (Dahrasena 455, Vyaghrasena 480, Madhyamasena 504, Vikramasena 533) argue that the Konkan was not wholly Vakataka before Harishena (c. 480-510).

ledger.note: c. 388: the Traikutakas appear in Aparanta and southern Gujarat. Infobox "Established: c. 388 CE"; "The dominions of the Traikutakas further included Aparanta and northern Maharashtra." The first named king, Indradatta, is dated 415-440 and "known only from coins minted under his son", so the page leaves 388-415 empty. Predecessor on the infobox: Western Satraps.

ledger.note: c. 550: the Traikutaka line ends with Vikramasena. "the dynasty ended 'around AD 550' when he died" (Vikramasena, dated A.D. 533); the infobox says "Disestablished: c. 456" and the Harishena page "seems to have come to an end around 495", so three pages give three ends. The Traikutakas were "probably reduced to vassal status under the Vishnukundins" after Harishena's invasion in Madhyamasena's reign (undated).

wars.name: Vakataka invasion of the Traikutakas under Harishena

zones.text: the territories of the Traikutakas around the northern Konkan

wars.outcome: Harishena invaded in the reign of Madhyamasena (dated A.D. 504); the line was then probably reduced to vassals of the Vishnukundinas.
wars.note: The years are Harishena's reign (c. 480-510, from the Harishena page: "Reign: c. 480 - 510"; death "in about 510"); the Traikutaka page gives no year for the invasion, and the Harishena page claims Lata and Trikuta among his conquests without a date. No contest is drawn because no campaign year is given.

certainty.note: No border is given; the extent is the coin-find area (Aparanta, southern Gujarat, northern Maharashtra).

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks. Three pages opened (budget 2-5). The end differs by page: infobox c. 456, Harishena page c. 495 ("seems to have come to an end"), Traikutaka text "around AD 550" with kings dated to 533; 550 is used because it is the only one consistent with the dated king list. The start (c. 388) is the infobox's; the first dated king is 415. The Traikutaka era question (249 or the Shaka era) is a chronology matter and moves no border. The relation to the Abhiras (Abhira-Traikutakas) is a theory the page reports; this dossier keeps them separate and the Abhira dossier ends at 370. The Vishnukundina vassalage is undated and not drawn; vishnukundina-dynasty has no dossier (sa-02-d asked sa-03). Overlaps: Cliopatria draws the Vakataka over 202 of this dossier's 368 cells from 451 and the Gupta over 163 in 410-450; this dossier's region overlaps both; whoever reconciles should read the Traikutaka dates, which put the dynasty in the Konkan to 504 and 533. Successor slugs kalachuris-of-mahishmati and mauryas-of-puri need dossiers (sa-03). Gazetteer names needed: Aparanta is an alias of Konkan, but Lata, Trikuta are not entries.
